technical_conclusions.developer_experience: Default provider/server factories and package-transitive generators supply static registration; optional DI/Hosting/protocol packages and advanced maintainer SPI do not impose global initialization, raw handles, duplicate model registration or consumer Cargo. Minimal and advanced strongly typed examples are design-compiled and explicitly unimplemented product APIs.
technical_conclusions.orm_and_aot: Typed Table/Column/Projection/Fluent/query tokens and explicit ordinary C# models retain the original ORM objective. The native engine owns AST/dialects/execution/relations; generated or equivalent handwritten static metadata is AOT-safe. Normal Entity/DTO/Handler edits do not require rd.xml, manual reflection preservation, runtime expression compilation or a per-model Rust build.
technical_conclusions.ownership_and_mapping: The common operation/owner protocol is precise through success, cancellation, timeout, failure, take, retirement and release. Relation and Server repairs resolve concrete cross-domain transport/liveness gaps; public task completion is never treated as native quiescence.
technical_conclusions.package_independence: Core is BCL-only and loads no native runtime alone. Providers and Server are separately consumable; the Query namespace lives in Database to avoid an assembly cycle. Optional protocol managed packages share one explicitly disclosed native Server closure. Native loading, managed-code extension and hot replacement are distinct.

technical_conclusions.limits_and_performance: Buffer/staging/codec/metadata/queue/native-runtime costs are stated and bounded where promised; payload limits are not process-RSS guarantees. Near-native speed, pristine-machine consumption, full product AOT behavior, real-service soak and release readiness require the existing Delivery evidence.

contract_reviews.rationale: Stable .NET11.0.0/SDK11.0.100 and C#15 are explicit and independently checked against official release/language sources. Required Linux/Windows x64 AOT evidence, normal linker prerequisites and future mobile/static-link limits are distinguished. Historical toolchain runs remain at their actual versions.

Fixed-width versioned records, layout probes, bootstrap capacity rules and success-only owner transfer are coherent. Shared error records, checked lengths and domain operation contracts avoid exposing Rust layout, exceptions, trait objects or application-owned raw handles.

The minimal binding inventory, static LibraryImport/UCO routes and deterministic generator/analyzer responsibilities are precise. Model/DTO/handler variation is managed source and bounded native data; no peer-generator output dependency, runtime query compiler or default Rust rebuild is required.

Logical close and physical leases are separate; admitted native use, parent/child dependencies, take-once outputs and callback retirement retain the creating module. Private SafeHandle ownership and guarded wrapper adoption avoid raw-owner leaks. Domain relation/cache and retained Server chunk repairs are consistent.

Registration publication, revoke, native callback quiescence and queued managed delivery retirement are distinct. Static entry points retain cookies until every relevant guard retires, forbid exceptions across FFI, and avoid user continuations under native locks or callback frames.

Create/register/start, single immutable terminal outcome, cancellation acknowledgement, take-once results and asynchronous retirement are specified separately. Synchronous completion/start races and cancellation-registration disposal are accounted for; Task completion does not falsely certify zero remote effects or reclamation.

Owned buffers and scoped readers prevent ordinary safe-code lifetime escape; copy APIs state allocations, bounded staging and cancellation/partial-write behavior. Length/extent arithmetic, actual backing-capacity accounting and transferred Server chunk anchors preserve ownership through close and deadline expiration.

Status/ErrorRecord capacity, original failure preservation, error owner release, UTF-8 bounds and managed exception translation are explicit. Pre-native failures do not fabricate native tuples; panic containment does not claim recovery from abort, corrupt pointers or fatal process failure.

Engine-local execution and finite admission/retirement quotas avoid a mandatory global runtime. Affinity and reentrancy are capabilities, and close does not substitute timeout for quiescence. Selected Server payload credit is explicitly nonwaiting while bounded queue/network waits remain separate.

Maintainer native builds and normal precompiled consumer builds are separated. Exact owned NuGet dependency closure, hard post-restore validation, unique native basenames, transitive generator assets and immutable publication/upgrade rules are concrete; packaging evidence is scoped and clean-machine/release gates remain explicit.

A small capability-based Core supports independent synchronous codec and asynchronous HTTP integration without domain algorithms or a common runtime. Explicit static engine descriptors, process-resident module identity and separate trusted maintainer SPI preserve AOT and package independence.

Finite models, source inspection, compilation, real AOT execution and later product verification have distinct claims. Exact current/source snapshots, scoped independent reports, attributable attestations and unchanged-input rebind rules now fail closed, with focused negative cases and preserved historical gates.

The methodology compares equivalent end-to-end native/facade/.NET paths, counts FFI/allocation/copy/pin/queue/runtime/diagnostic costs, distinguishes retained bytes from RSS and requires uncertainty/resource correctness. No unexecuted performance win or production resource bound is claimed.

Future GPU/UI/mobile/media capabilities retain engine-specific affinity, lifecycle, linking and device/fence requirements. Runtime native loading is separate from managed-code extension and hot replacement; the standard/scaffold requires explicit adoption and does not promise unsupported future platforms.
